Done — the entry is in `CHANGELOG.md:20`. Here's what I found and the calls I made.

## The shape of the release

380 commits, of which **37** are `feat`/`fix`/`perf`. The rest is 153 `chore`, 73 `refactor`, 64 `test`, 33 `ci`, 20 `docs`. The merged-PR sheet is a strict subset of the commit log — it's missing 17 user-facing commits, including `fix(http): close the pool on shutdown` and `fix(db): guard the null cursor in the paginator`. **Don't write the notes off the PR sheet.**

Most repeated messages are the same fix applied across modules — "guard the null cursor in the paginator" lands in api, db, queue, and webhooks; "drop the duplicate header" in five places. I collapsed those into one user-facing line each rather than listing them per-module.

## The thing to look at first

**`fix(auth): return 401 for an expired token instead of 403`** is filed as a fix but it's a breaking change. Anyone branching on 403 to detect an expired session silently stops detecting it. I put it under Breaking.

Two more breaking changes are hiding under `refactor:`:

- **`stop re-exporting the internal error types`** (8 commits across auth, billing, core, db, jobs) — that's a removal from the public export surface. Anyone `instanceof`-checking those breaks at import.
- **`drop the unused v1 export route`** — the author says "unused," but that's a route removal. It touched `router.js`, `handlers.js`, and the tests, so it was really wired up.

## What I left out, and why

**All 10 `perf` commits.** Your template is fixed at three headings, and perf fits none of them honestly. Substantively they're micro-optimizations — "avoid the extra clone in the mapper," "skip the JSON round-trip on the hot path" — with no benchmark numbers anywhere in the history, so there's no claim a user would notice. The one I'd reconsider is `perf(api): reuse the parsed schema between requests`. Say the word and I'll add a Performance section.

Also out: 13× "drop the unused v2 debug helper," 10× "delete the dead feature-flag branch," the `Ctx`→`RequestCtx` rename (explicitly internal, and now unreachable anyway given the re-export removal), and every dep bump — all patch/minor.

## Three things to verify before you cut

1. **Minimum Node version.** Five `ci: run the suite on node 22`, four `docs: note the minimum node version`, three `.nvmrc` pins — but no `engines` bump in any commit's diffstat. If `engines` actually moved, that's a Breaking line I haven't written. There's no `package.json` here so I couldn't check.
2. **`refactor(*): pull the request id out of the logger context`** (db, http, queue, store). Reads either as "removed it from the log line" or "hoisted it into its own field." The first is a breaking change for anyone parsing your logs; the second is invisible. I left it out rather than guess wrong — worth 30 seconds with the diff.
3. **The date.** I used 2026-08-28 for tomorrow's cut, but the history ends 2026-06-17. If that ten-week gap means there are commits not in this log, the digest is incomplete.
